SMTO-AUT-0041 — This sign-in needs a saved connection with an https:// address

GUID: f8e0668c-b559-5da6-9e71-9bac0619bbac
Slug: auth-secure-transport-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth

What happened

  • SMTO only sends this kind of sign-in through a connection saved in Parameter Store whose address starts with https://. This request used an unsaved connection or a plain http:// address, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, find the saved connection SMTO should use, and check that its Base URL starts with https:// rather than http://. SMTO only attaches this kind of sign-in to secure addresses, so a plain http:// address is refused.
  2. If there's no saved connection for this service, ask the person who manages SMTO to create one with an https:// address and its sign-in settings. This sign-in can't be used with an address typed into a single request; it has to belong to a saved connection.
  3. In the conversation, ask SMTO to repeat the request using that saved connection by name. Naming the saved connection makes SMTO use its secure address and its sign-in, and nothing was sent the first time.

What success looks like

  • The request goes through and SMTO shows the service's response instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change the address to http:// to get around this; the sign-in would travel unprotected.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP skill refused an auth_ref (OAuth) credential because the request did not use a saved Parameter Store HTTP connection, or that connection's base_url is not HTTPS.

What this means

  • auth_ref requires an existing saved HTTPS profile; an unsaved profile or non-HTTPS base URL cannot satisfy private authenticated egress. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • auth_ref requires an existing saved HTTPS profile; an unsaved profile or non-HTTPS base URL cannot satisfy private authenticated egress.

How to diagnose it

  • Check that the authentication reference belongs to an existing saved profile with an HTTPS base URL.

How to fix it

  • Use auth_ref only with a saved http_connection record whose base_url scheme is https (HttpRequestCapability._execute in src/agent_runtime/skills/http/request.py). Select or create that record in Parameter Store and reference it from the request; do not fall back to plaintext HTTP or inline auth.
  • Select or configure the intended saved HTTPS profile before using auth_ref credentials; do not substitute plaintext transport.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended saved HTTPS profile reaches the supported private credential broker.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
